purpose: Lysine is an essential amino acid that your body cannot make on its own, so you need to get it from food or supplements. It is most commonly used to help prevent and shorten cold sore outbreaks caused by the herpes simplex virus. It is also used to support protein building in the body, help with calcium absorption, and promote overall health.
how_it_works: The herpes virus needs another amino acid called arginine to grow and multiply. Lysine works by competing with arginine and blocking the virus from getting the fuel it needs to cause an outbreak. Think of it like taking away the virus's food supply so it has a harder time causing those painful cold sores. It also helps your body build proteins needed for healthy muscles, bones, and tissues.
common_side_effects: Lysine is generally very well tolerated. Some people may experience mild stomach upset, nausea, diarrhea, or stomach cramps, especially when taking higher doses. These effects are usually temporary and mild.
warnings: Do not take very high doses without talking to your doctor first, as extremely large amounts may raise cholesterol levels or affect kidney function over time. If you have kidney disease or liver disease, check with your doctor before using lysine supplements. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult their healthcare provider before taking lysine. It may interact with calcium supplements or certain antibiotics, so let your pharmacist know all the medications and supplements you are taking.
typical_dosing: For cold sore prevention, a common dose is 1,000 mg (1 gram) taken one to three times daily. During an active cold sore outbreak, some people take up to 3,000 mg per day for a short period. Always follow the directions on the product label or your healthcare provider's instructions. Take it with food if it upsets your stomach.
